In Section 5, Rep. Noel opted to delete the last portion of Section 5 regarding the preferential rights of government employeesâ€™ cooperatives to operate revenue-generating activities in available government-owned sites and facilities, said Section 5 to now read, as follows:

â€œSEC. 6. Experts from the GFIs shall be called upon to conduct lectures, workshops in capacity building for entrepreneurship skills and live case studies of successful entrepreneurs. Participants shall be taught to identify and evaluate opportunities for new ventures and to understand how the capital investment process works. All GFIs shall set aside funds for this purpose: Provided, That financing of the entrepreneurial projects of retired government employees shall be dependent on the strength and quality of the proposed enterpriseâ€™s project and business cash flows, overall credit worthiness and other mitigating measures, in accordance with safe and sound banking practices, where applicable.â€�

The TWG likewise  agreed to adopt the recommendation of LBP on Section 7 for the CSC to spearhead the coordination among government agencies for the preparation, implementation and monitoring of a comprehensive plan for the government employees entrepreneurial development, as well as its funding sources, instead of creating a Council as provided for in the bill.  

Furthermore, Rep. Committee Chairman Peter Unabia stated that House Bill No. 5158 or the Pondo sa Pagbabago at Pag-asenso Bill (P3 bill) aims to replace the 5-6  money lending scheme and to make available a micro lending facility with an interest rate lower than the prevailing market rate.  If enacted into law, it will ensure the continuity of the P3 Program being implemented by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) through the Small Business Corporation (SB Corp.).
	In his sponsorship remarks, Rep. Gil Acosta cited the difficulty of the MSMEs  to access the credit programs for MSMEs due to high interest rate, and voluminous and stringent requirements, which is why they resort to borrowing from the â€œ5-6â€� micro lending scheme.   
	Mr. Melvin Abanto, Senior Vice President of the SB Corp., informed the Committee that the P3 Program was rolled out in three pilot areas, namely,  Mindoro, Sarangani and Tacloban.  The Committee requested the DTI to submit a status report on the roll-out in the three pilot provinces, and the guidelines for the P3 Program.

	Dir. Jerry Clavesillas of the Bureau of Micro, Small, Medium Enterprise Development  (BMSMED) of the DTI stated that other countries have a budget allocation for microfinancing. He emphasized that through the P3 Act, micro lending will be institutionalized and it will be mandatory for the government to lend out to the micro enterprise sector. Ms. Pia Bernandette Roman-Tayag of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) informed the body that microfinancing has long been promoted by the BSP and that 168 banks are engaged therein.

	The representatives from the DTI, BSP, Rural Bankers Association of the Philippines (RBAP), Chamber of Thrift Bank (CTB) and Microfinance Council of the Philippines, Inc. (MCPI) expressed their support for the passage of the measure. 

	Among the other comments and suggestions given by the resource persons are:  (a) need to strengthen the guarantee facility because of the risk of lending to micro enterprises;  and (b) perception that loans to micro enterprises are dole-outs, accounting for the low repayment rate.
	Rep. Angelina Tan suggested that the P3 loans be given to the poorest populations, instead of the poorest provinces. 
	The Committee agreed to convene a technical working group, to be chaired by Rep. Tan, to fine-tune the provisions of the bill.

The TWG agreed on the following amendments: 

1.	On Section 2 (Declaration of Policy): Insert the phrase â€œand programsâ€� after the word â€œplansâ€�.

2.	On Section 3 (Objectives):
 a) In paragraph (a), the Secretariat was directed to find another term for    â€œhassle-freeâ€�.  Change â€œpoorest provincesâ€� to â€œpoorest populationsâ€�  where the P3 Program will be made available, as suggested by Rep. Tan;
 b)  In paragraph (b), change the word â€œreplaceâ€� with the phrase â€œprovide a      better alternative toâ€� in referring to informal lenders. 
   
3.	On Section 6 (Features of the P3 Fund):  Instead of specifying the loanable amount and minimal interest rate, the TWG proposed  that â€œThe loanable amount for individual loans, and the interest rate to the conduits and to the end beneficiaries shall be set and regularly reviewed by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development (MSMED) Council: Provided,That the interest rate shall be lower than the prevailing interest rate charged by the micro finance institutions (MFIs)â€�, and that â€œThe interest earnings shall accrue to the P3 Fundâ€�.  

4.	On Section 7 (Policy Oversight Function):  Clarified that the MSMED Council shall perform â€œpolicyâ€� oversight functions on the P3 Fund; and that the MSMED Council shall â€œsubmit to the President and to Congress, through the Congressional Oversight Committee on Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development (COC-MSMED), a yearly report on the status of the P3 Fundâ€�.

	SB Corp. was requested to craft the revised language for the Appropriations Section and submit the same to the Secretariat.
	
	The Secretariat was directed to prepare and e-mail the draft substitute bill reflecting the amendments based on the discussions and agreements arrived at by the TWG.  The TWG participants were requested to review the same and submit their comments thereon the following week.

rows.title_short: “ The Urban Agriculture Act Of 2017 ”
rows.abstract: Defines the terms “Urban Agriculture” and “Vertical Farming”; Involves the application of intensive production methods such as the using and reusing of urban sources and wastes; Also involves animal husbandry aquaculture, agro-forestry and horticulture; Employs the concepts of indoor agriculture in skyscrapers and other modern buildings; Integrates these methods in the academic curriculum of Institutions studying courses on Agriculture; Practical Arts, Home Economics, etc., and also incorporates its concept in the NSTP or the CMT.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE COMMISSION ON HIGHER EDUCATION TO INCLUDE A SUBJECT OF MORO HISTORY, CULTURE AND IDENTITY STUDIES AS AN ELECTIVE IN THE HIGHER EDUCATION CURRICULUM
rows.abstract: Acknowledges that education plays an important role in recognizing the value of interdependence among cultures; Proposes therefore to promote greater appreciation of centuries-long rich historical and cultural heritage among majority of Filipinos by recognizing the rightful place of the Bangsamoro people in the fabric of our national history; Aims to help instill in the consciousness and understanding of the Filipino students the Muslim culture which may possibly eradicate certain biases instilled in the minds of individuals; Emphasizes, among others the positive relations and remembrances in history among the tri-people of Mindanao:  the Christian settlers and their descendants, the Moros or Muslims and the Lumads or indigenous highland tribes.
